title: LCM and HCF: Factors, Multiples, and Their Powers

questions.question: What are HCF(12, 18) and LCM(12, 18)?
questions.rationale: Common factors of 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6 — the highest is 6. The first shared multiple is 36. Check: 6 × 36 = 216 = 12 × 18.

questions.question: Using prime factorisation, what is HCF(24, 36)?
questions.rationale: 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3²; the HCF takes the lowest power of each common prime: 2² × 3 = 12.

questions.question: Using prime factorisation, what is LCM(24, 36)?
questions.rationale: The LCM takes the highest power of each prime seen: 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72. The golden relation confirms it: 12 × 72 = 864 = 24 × 36.

questions.question: For which numbers does the relation HCF × LCM = product of the numbers hold?
questions.rationale: The relation is valid only for two numbers. It fails for three: HCF(2, 3, 4) = 1 and LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12, but 1 × 12 ≠ 24.

questions.question: Two bells toll every 6 s and 8 s, starting together. After how many seconds do they next toll together?
questions.rationale: "Together again" signals the LCM: 6 = 2 × 3 and 8 = 2³, so LCM = 2³ × 3 = 24 seconds.

questions.question: A rectangular floor is 24 m by 36 m. What is the side of the largest square tile that fits exactly, with no cutting?
questions.rationale: "Largest measure dividing exactly" signals the HCF. HCF(24, 36) = 12, so 12 m tiles cover the floor as 2 × 3 = 6 tiles.

questions.question: In the division ladder method, the LCM equals:
options: Product of the common divisors only
Product of divisors and the leftover co-prime bottoms
The larger of the two numbers
questions.rationale: For 24 and 36 the ladder divides by 2, 2, 3 (divisors) leaving 2 and 3; LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 2 × 3 = 72, while HCF = divisors only = 12.

questions.question: The numbers 4 and 9 are co-prime. Their LCM is:
questions.rationale: Co-prime numbers have HCF 1, so their LCM is simply their product: 4 × 9 = 36.

questions.question: Which statement is always true?
options: The LCM is smaller than both numbers
questions.rationale: The HCF divides each number, and each number divides the LCM, so the HCF must divide the LCM — e.g. 12 divides 72 for 24 and 36.

questions.question: Two runners start together on a circular track and take 60 s and 90 s per lap. When do they next meet at the start line together?
questions.rationale: Meeting together on a circular track is an LCM question: LCM(60, 90) = 180 seconds — the same mathematics as bells tolling together.
